(1) Signers whose limits are Some({token -> None}) or None (smart-wallet-interface/src/types.rs:70-72 and smart-wallet/src/context.rs:33 `None => return true`) authorize any

failing_checks.title: Cumulative budget
failing_checks.reason: The only amount control is per call. policy__ has no running total. The only state is the Installed(wallet) marker written at sample-policy/src/lib.rs:75, and that stores no spend. So many calls of 10M each all pass.

failing_checks.title: Recipient binding
failing_checks.reason: The policy checks no destination. It reads args[2] only and never args[1], the `to` address. Any recipient is approved, and the recipient is chosen by whoever builds the transaction. The value is not limited to an operator-fixed or allowlisted payee.

failing_checks.title: Asset identity and units
failing_checks.reason: The asset is never identified. The policy accepts the `contract` of any transfer by function name only, with no code, issuer or contract-id check. The amount is a raw i128 under one cap, with no decimals or per-asset scaling. The value checked is the value signed, but the asset is not identified at

failing_checks.title: Failure and rollback paths
failing_checks.reason: Rejected or failed auth paths revert atomically (__check_auth returns Err or panics, and add_signer's install panic aborts the add), so there is no partial debit. The failing path is in remove_signer (lib.rs:104-137), which deletes the signer record but does not reconcile the policy's Installed mark

failing_checks.title: Verification of incoming authentication
failing_checks.reason: For a required Policy co-signer, the wallet only checks expiry if the key is still stored (context.rs:112). If the policy was removed from the wallet, it is no longer stored, so no check runs and the policy still approves via policy__ (context.rs:121-130). Policy__ does not check current membership;
